messages:
Sasha: Heads-up: staging p95 +40% after today's merge (model v4.3 onboarding). Looks like a perf regression during generation.
Kevin: Which metric specifically? p95 tokens/sec or end-to-end latency?
Sasha: end-to-end p95 latency for short prompt workloads (avg prompt len ~12 tokens). See quick profiler snippet below.
Kevin: paste the profiler
Sasha: ```
profile: staging-run-2026-03-18
hotspots:
  kernel_selector: 34.6%  # up from ~8%
  kv_cache_evictions: 18.2%  # spike correlated with rollout
  batching_fallback: 22.1%  # many single-request batches
notes: tokenizer.normalizer changed in PR #345abc
```
Maria: CI perf job also failed on the perf/regression suite — flagged by ci-bot: FAIL p95_latency_generation > threshold
CI-bot: [perf/regression] job failed: p95_generation_latency ↑ 38% (baseline: 82ms, current: 113ms) — see https://ci.internal/perf/9876
Jonah: this smells like two interacting changes: tokenizer mapping changed token lengths -> kernel selector chooses different kernel (more fallback to generic kernel) -> smaller batches + KV churn
Kevin: I ran a quick bisect on the staging image. The change landed with merge commit 345abc -> 346def. Reverting 345abc locally restores p95 to baseline.
Lucy: KV metrics show eviction rate jumped at the same time: median KV cache lifetime dropped from 12s -> 1.6s. Likely tokenization produced more fragment keys.
Sasha: also seeing scheduler fall back to policy 'latency-first' -> single-request scheduling for these prompts. That increases per-token overhead.
Kevin: repro steps I used:
```bash
# run perf harness
perf-run --model v4.3 --profile staging-small-prompts --compare baseline
# bisect range
git bisect start HEAD origin/main~6
git bisect run ./perf-fast-check.sh
```
Kevin: bisect points to tokenizer normalizer + prefetch heuristic tweak in onboard-manager
Maria: Can we hold the rollout? UX: rollout controller hasn't auto-rolled back because capacity SLOs still ok, but perf SLOs breached. Request: pause canary and pin previous model variant for staging.
Sasha: @Ops-bot can you hold the canary and pin model to v4.2 in staging?
Ops-bot: command received: hold-rollout staging canary; pin model v4.2 -> success :white_check_mark:
Kevin: Quick mitigation: pin tokenizer config to previous normalization (normalize_unicode: false) and force kernel_selector policy 'stable-v2' until further analysis.
Maria: Created issue PERF-1123 with perf graphs and links. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml. https://issues.internal/PRJ/PERF-1123
Jonah: Next steps: 1) reproduce minimal unit test that shows kernel selection flip; 2) instrument kernel selector decision path with token-length histogram; 3) evaluate prefetcher keyization for tokenizer mapping.
Lucy: Also add KV cache TTL tuning to limit eviction thrash as temporary guard.
Kevin: I'll prepare a small revert PR for just the tokenizer normalizer change (345abc revert) and a hotfix to pin kernel selector policy. Will request urgent review.
Sasha: thanks — holding canary and opening a short window for rollback. After revert + hotfix we should run perf/regression suite and then re-enable canary if green. :pray:
Maria: Add postmortem note in the issue when resolved. Also schedule a short async sync with eng-ml tomorrow to avoid config drift on onboard merges.
Kevin: FYI CI-bot also captured perf artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/staging/2825012345/
CI-bot: perf artifacts archived successfully.
Sasha: closing loop: keep this thread updated with PR links and perf numbers. If anyone tests locally, drop numbers here. :mag:
